claims.text: Increasing the volume fraction of Cr-rich nanoprecipitates in a FeNiCrCoCu coating will improve wear resistance during high-temperature sliding.
Increasing the volume fraction of Cr-rich nanoprecipitates will reduce microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding.
Cr-rich nanoprecipitates enhance grain-boundary cohesion in FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
Cr-rich nanoprecipitates retard thermally activated grain-boundary sliding.
The baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating has a homogeneous microstructure.
Adjusted thermal treatment can increase the formation and distribution of Cr-rich nanoprecipitates.
A slight increase in Cr content relative to the baseline can increase the formation and distribution of Cr-rich nanoprecipitates.
Grain-boundary sliding is activated in the intended high-temperature sliding regime.
The relevant Cr-rich nanoprecipitates are located at or near grain boundaries.
Pinning grain boundaries suppresses thermally activated grain-boundary sliding.
Suppressing grain-boundary sliding reduces localized plasticity.
Reduced localized plasticity leads to lower wear rates and diminished microscopic deformation.
The modified coating will have a lower wear rate than the baseline coating under high-temperature sliding.
The modified coating will exhibit less microstructural deformation than the baseline coating under high-temperature sliding.
The predictions cease to be expected when severe oxidation or substrate-diffusion effects dominate wear behavior.
A failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in both wear rate and microscopic deformation, or observation of worse performance, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
